_readme: Reviewed (unit, code) pairs for Quantities emitted against the UCUM system.
Key format is "<unit>|<code>", where unit is the human-readable Quantity.unit
and code is the machine-readable Quantity.code. '(none)' means Quantity.unit
was absent, which is itself usually a defect.
status 'approved' -> a human confirmed the unit and the code describe the same
quantity, and that this is what the source API actually sends.
status 'rejected' -> the pair is wrong. Fails the gate with the recorded reason.
Anything absent  -> unreviewed. Fails the gate.
The rejected entries below were verified during the July 2026 assessment.
The rest of the repository's pairs are deliberately absent so the gate fails
until each one is signed off. Do not bulk-approve.
"unitless" records Quantities that carry a value and deliberately no unit, keyed
by file. A missing unit is normally a defect, so an entry here needs a reason and
an occurrence count. The count is the guard: it is checked exactly, so adding a
new bare Quantity to a waived file fails the gate rather than inheriting the
sign-off written for a different one. Keying by line was rejected — a line number
drifts under any edit above it and the waiver would quietly move to another
Quantity. A waiver that matches nothing is stale and also fails.

steps|steps.reason: 'steps' is not a UCUM code. UCUM expresses countable things as annotations.
steps|steps.suggested: unit 'steps', code '{steps}'. The same file already uses {score} and {count} correctly.

MET-min|min.reason: MET-minutes is not minutes. A receiver reading code 'min' interprets 300 MET-minutes as 300 minutes of activity.
MET-min|min.suggested: There is no UCUM code for MET-min. Use an annotation such as '{MET-min}', or emit the value under a vendor-local system.

degree|deg.reason: UCUM Table 5 defines deg as [pi].rad/360, so 'degree'/'deg' is a correct pair. This entry was previously 'rejected', but what it actually flagged was a DATA defect, not a unit defect: VITRONIC emitted radian values under it. That conversion now happens in provider-vitronic (radiansToDegrees), so the pair itself is sound.
degree|deg.guarded_by: A unit gate cannot detect a value in the wrong scale — 1.48 deg is structurally perfect. The guard against a regression is numeric: provider-vitronic asserts a known angle reads ~84.89 degrees, and fhir-core asserts 1 rad converts to 57.2957795 deg via @lhncbc/ucum-lhc. If those tests are ever deleted, this pair loses its protection.
degree|deg.reviewed: 2026-07-26, verified against the UCUM specification Table 5

\u00b0C|Cel.reason: Used for a temperature deviation, not an absolute temperature. UCUM 'Cel' denotes a point on the Celsius scale; a difference is 'K'.

meter|m.reason: Applied to cross-section AREA values, which are emitted as 'm2' at the top level of the same resource. The same number appears twice, once as an area and once as a length.
meter|m.suggested: Areas are 'm2' throughout. Remove the length-coded duplicates.

packages/provider-vitronic/src/fhir/mapp.reason: VITRONIC BodyLoop scan properties are untyped key/value pairs and the API states no unit for them anywhere in the payload. The mapper emits the number with no unit rather than asserting a UCUM unit nobody has verified, which ground rule 1 forbids and which would be the worse error: a wrong unit is silently interpretable, a missing one is visibly incomplete. FHIR permits a Quantity with only a value, and the HL7 validator reports no error on the emitted bundle.
packages/provider-vitronic/src/fhir/mapp.resolved_by: A reviewed property_path -> unit table, tracked as TODO(clinical-review) in the mapper. Once it exists the paths with a known unit carry one and this waiver shrinks or goes away.
packages/provider-vitronic/src/fhir/mapp.reviewed: Martin Etzrodt, PhD, Open Science Foundation, 2026-07-26
